drafts.title: Lightweight Hallucination Detection in RAG Pipelines with LettuceDetect: Practical Tradeoffs?
drafts.body: Hallucinations remain a major challenge in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, especially in sensitive domains like medicine and law (F1). Existing detection methods often struggle with context window limits, notably in encoder-only models (F2), or incur high inference costs when relying on LLMs (F3). LettuceDetect is an open-source, encoder-based tool built on ModernBERT that flags hallucinated spans in LLM-generated answers without needing an LLM, handling up to 4K tokens (F4, F5). It reportedly achieves 79.22% F1 on the RAGTruth benchmark (F6) and is MIT licensed with Python packages and a Hugging Face demo available (F7). However, details on its real-time detection capabilities, training data, and comparative performance against other lightweight detectors remain unclear. For those working with local RAG setups or lightweight hallucination evaluation, how viable is an encoder-based approach like LettuceDetect for real-time or near-real-time detection? What practical limitations or integration challenges have you encountered or anticipate?
